newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Castrol, chemicals to fuel Burmah.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Castrol, chemicals to fuel Burmah.

text.p: Burmah Castrol's first-half results, due out on Monday, will have calmly motored ahead, fuelled by growth in its Castrol lubricants and an improved chemicals result, analysts said.
Their forecasts for net income centre around 65 million stg, up from a clean 57.5 million stg a year ago.
"Essentially it is normal growth in lubricants and cost cutting in chemicals, while a lower fuels contribution will be offset by lower interest charges," said Nick Antill at BZW.
Burmah pulled out of the competitive fuels retailing sector in Chile, Sweden and Turkey earlier in the year.
It had already disposed of its UK fuels business in 1995.
This year's divestments have led to a one-off gain of 20 million stg, which is not included in analysts' estimates.
Burmah, which stuck to its fuel retailing activities in Australia, Belgium and Ireland, is focusing on its core lubricants and chemicals businesses.
Lubricants made up nearly 70 percent of 1995's operating profit and are set to become more important as Burmah is building on the strong Castrol brand name in fast growing Asian markets.
The outlook in the mature European market, however, has become more grim following the merger of the European downstream aseets of British Petroleum and Mobil Corp.
While this link will probably only begin to make an impact next year, first-half profit growth will likely have been held back by cold winter weather, analysts said.
Chilly temperatures hurt lubricant sales as people drive less, said Irene Himona at SG Strauss Turnbull. Adverse exchange rates will also have helped dampen the profit rise, she added.
"These two negatives will have impacted earnings growth," Himona said.
Burmah's niche position in chemicals will have safeguarded it against the hard times experienced by bulk producers.
Restructuring and its focus on specialty products will instead have boosted chemicals results, analysts said. Over 20 percent of last year's operating profit stemmed from chemicals.
Burmah Castrol's shares have made strong advances earlier this month, climbing from 988 pence on August 6 to 1,052 pence today, with analysts seeing scope for more long-term gains.
"It's got a valuable niche position, it's making very strong growth in emerging markets and frankly the share ratings are quite undemanding," said Himona.
